nominal_scale.kind: nominal art-direction choice, not a newly measured fossil dimension; display scaling separately labeled

budget_intent.policy: 14k triangles and 1,000,000 bytes are ceilings, not targets. Usually aim about 100–500 KB; below this range is fine. Spend more triangles only for visible silhouette/proportion/connection benefit. Do not pad counts or enlarge textures for apparent refinement. Preserve quality if a justified asset exceeds the usual range within the hard caps.

start_gate: Next round is planning only; parent explicit exclusive assignment needed. For already assigned workers, latest state and explicit parent dispatch override stale empty claims or initial queue snapshots.
concurrency: Parent-coordinated shared host pool; default one worker x two Blender threads, no per-batch full-host allocation.

design.observed: Thick continuous layered ash block, sparse rounded aggregates emerging from top and front, a few concentric section faces. Broad matrix areas remain quiet. Number and location of sectioned pellets differ between panels; surface speckle is illustrative.
design.resolve: Freeze one original continuous ash block with quiet top, seven subtly uneven layers, small embedded rounded pellets, and three intentionally exposed concentric section faces. Deposition layers wrap continuously; aggregate scales/bands are illustrative enlarged teaching features, not specimen measurements. Do not copy image speckle as a texture.
design.masses: Irregular clipped-corner eroded block, closed bottom and broad ash-matrix strata; small rounded faceted embedded pellets. Concentric section geometry sits flush against front/right matrix faces. Palette-only portable material regions.

structural_revision: Original ImageGen reused. Replace flat open circular section inlays with actual closed truncated spherical aggregates; visible convex flanks behind each cut face establish embedded grain volume. Increase selected exposed top pellets while keeping continuous ash matrix dominant. Reduce layer color contrast to avoid cake-like striping.
